# ScreenVault — Landing Page Build Instructions

## Overview

Build a single-page landing site for **ScreenVault**, a massive UI/UX design inspiration library (400,000+ screenshots). The audience is product designers and design teams who need fast reference material. The page must convert visitors into free or paid users by demonstrating the library's depth, powerful search, and workflow integrations.

## Tone & Visual Direction

Think **clean, contemporary SaaS** — generous whitespace, crisp typography, and a neutral palette (white/off-white backgrounds, near-black text, subtle grays). Use a single vibrant accent color (electric blue or violet) for CTAs and interactive highlights. Typography should feel premium: a geometric or grotesque sans-serif (Inter, General Sans, or similar). Rounded corners on cards and pills; soft shadows. The overall mood is *"polished design tool"* — the site itself should feel like something a designer would respect.

## Key Priorities

1. **Interactions are the core experience.** The animated stat counters, search tab switching, filter pills, and flows toggle must feel responsive and polished — these demonstrate the product's power. Use smooth transitions (200–300ms easing) and make sure tab/filter state changes are visually obvious.

2. **Testimonials & brand marquees** should create a sense of momentum — continuous, buttery-smooth horizontal scrolling that reinforces social proof without requiring user effort.

3. **Stats section** needs to land with impact. The counting animation should trigger on scroll-into-view and feel satisfying (ease-out, staggered start).

4. **Responsive design is non-negotiable.** The screenshot grids, filter pill rows, and multi-row testimonial carousels must gracefully adapt from desktop to mobile.

5. **Hero clarity** — the headline, one-liner, and dual CTAs ("Join for free" + "See our plans") must be immediately scannable above the fold.

Refer to `task_input.json` for the full section order, interaction specs, data values, and navigation definitions.

---

## Data Sources

1. Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md` for all content materials (text, data).
2. Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json` for structural requirements, data placement, and interaction definitions.

## Output Requirements

1. Output all files to `/app/output/`. `index.html` must be the main entry point.
2. All pages must be openable directly in a browser (no build step needed). Use relative paths for inter-page links.

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — make professional judgments autonomously. Do not pause, ask questions, or wait for replies.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies `site.tone`, `site.audience`, etc., use them to choose styles, layouts, and color schemes. Otherwise, make professional judgments.
3. **Priority** — these rules override any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The skill's workflow, quality standards, and technical specs remain fully effective — only skip interactive waits.
I'll start by reading the data sources, then invoke the frontend-design-ultimate skill.

1	# ScreenVault — UI & UX design inspiration for mobile & web apps
2	
3	## Brand
4	ScreenVault is a comprehensive design inspiration library for UI/UX designers, product designers, and design teams. It offers a fully searchable collection of mobile and web app screenshots, user flows, and UI elements to accelerate design research and decision-making. The tone is modern, minimal, and professional.
5	
6	Brand colors: #141414 (primary dark), #FFFFFF (background white), #F5F5F5 (light gray surface)
7	
8	## Announcement Bar
9	2025 ScreenVault Awards — Celebrating the best on the internet.
10	
11	## Hero Content
12	Title: Discover real-world design inspiration.
13	Subtitle: Featuring over 1,000 iOS & Web apps, and 200 sites — New content weekly.
14	Primary CTA: "Join for free"
15	Secondary CTA: "See our plans"
16	
17	Navigation links: Pricing · Awards · Log in
18	
19	## Social Proof
20	Trusted by design teams at: (display as logo row of well-known tech/design companies)
21	
22	## Library Statistics
23	A growing library of:
24	- **1,150** apps
25	- **615,900** screens
26	- **329,200** flows
27	
28	These numbers animate with a counting effect when the section scrolls into view.
29	
30	## Search Categories
31	Filter pill categories available for browsing design patterns:
32	- Profile
33	- Wallet
34	- Welcome
35	- Account Setup
36	- Home
37	- Subscription & Paywall
38	- Login
39	- Settings
40	- Checkout
41	- Collections
42	
43	Pills are displayed in a horizontally scrollable row and update the screenshot grid when selected.
44	
45	## Feature Tabs
46	Tab navigation options within the search feature section:
47	- **Screens** — Browse full-screen captures of real apps
48	- **UI Elements** — Explore individual components and patterns
49	- **Flows** — View connected sequences of screens
50	- **Text in Screenshot** — Search by visible on-screen copy
51	
52	Clicking a tab switches the content area to show the corresponding search results view.
53	
54	## Feature: Search
55	**Find design patterns in seconds.**
56	The search feature section combines the tab navigation (Screens, UI Elements, Flows, Text in Screenshot) with filter pills to let users quickly narrow down relevant design references from the library. The grid of screenshot results updates dynamically based on the active tab and selected filter category.
57	
58	## Feature: Flows
59	**Explore entire user journeys with flows.**
60	
61	- **Videos** — Experience flows the way they were meant to be experienced, complete with transitions, micro-interactions, and animations.
62	- **Prototype mode** — Walk through flows, step by step, by using the interactive hotspots at your own preferred pace.
63	
64	A toggle switches between the Videos view and the Prototype mode view.
65	
66	## Inspiration Tools
67	**From inspiration to creation.**
68	
69	- **Copy to Figma** — Download designs you like or copy them straight into Figma with our new Figma plugin.
70	- **Save to collections** — Collect your favorite designs and upload your own screenshots into one place.
71	- **Leave comments** — Take notes upon saving so you'll never forget the context in the future.
72	
73	Each tool is presented as a feature card with a visual preview and short description.
74	
75	## Testimonials
76	**What our users are saying.**
77	
78	Displayed as a multi-row, auto-scrolling marquee carousel of testimonial cards.
79	
80	- **Sebastian Speier**, Shop — "ScreenVault is a great resource and it always comes in handy to see what the best practices or standards are for mobile patterns in our current landscape."
81	- **Meng To**, DesignCode — "ScreenVault is a game-changer for designers looking to step up their understanding of UX and UI design patterns. It's so massive, meticulously organized, has deep user flows and even a Figma plugin! It's indispensable in the modern designer's toolbox."
82	- **Marco Cornacchia**, Figma — "ScreenVault is one of my favorite resources for product design and UI inspo. I love having access to a ton of 'real world examples' to see how different apps and companies handle specific UI patterns and flows."
83	- **Daryl Ginn**, Endless — "ScreenVault has quickly become our favourite inspiration resource for designing mobile apps at endless.design, their advanced filtering is unmatched in the inspiration space."
84	- **Rachel How** — "ScreenVault is my go-to reference for app & web design. Apart from saving countless hours, it gives me insights on the design patterns, copywriting, and user flows of world-class products. A must-have for creative inspiration and efficiency!"
85	- **Haerin Song**, Visa — "By using the ScreenVault app, I save both my research time and space in my photo galleries filled with random screenshots. I love how easy it is to search for different patterns and copy and paste flows into Figma. It is a wonderful design tool you cannot live without!"
86	
87	## CTA Section
88	**Never run out of inspiration again.**
89	Use ScreenVault for free as long as you like or get full access with any of our paid plans.
90	
91	Primary CTA: "Join for free"
92	Secondary CTA: "See our plans"
93	
94	Below the CTA, rows of recognizable app icons scroll in a continuous horizontal marquee animation in alternating directions. Brands include: Coinbase, Wise, Headspace, Airbnb, Uber, Nike, Pinterest, ChatGPT, Shopify, Loom, Mailchimp, Twitch, Spotify, Apple TV, Notion, Dropbox.
95	
96	## Footer Navigation
97	**Tagline:** Design better digital experiences with ScreenVault.

{"type": "text", "text": "Base directory for this skill: /logs/agent/sessions/skills/frontend-design-ultimate

# Frontend Design Ultimate

Create distinctive, production-grade static sites from text requirements alone. No mockups, no Figma — just describe what you want and get bold, memorable designs.

**Stack**: React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui + Framer Motion  
**Output**: Vite (static HTML) or Next.js (Vercel-ready)

## Quick Start

```
"Build a SaaS landing page for an AI writing tool. Dark theme, 
editorial typography, subtle grain texture. Pages: hero with 
animated demo, features grid, pricing table, FAQ accordion, footer."
```

---

## Design Thinking (Do This First)

Before writing any code, commit to a **BOLD aesthetic direction**:

### 1. Understand Context

- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?
- **Audience**: Developer tools? Consumer app? Enterprise? Creative agency?
- **Constraints**: Performance requirements, accessibility needs, brand guidelines?

### 2. Choose an Extreme Tone

Pick ONE and commit fully — timid designs fail:

| Tone                       | Characteristics                                           |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Brutally Minimal**       | Sparse, monochrome, massive typography, raw edges         |
| **Maximalist Chaos**       | Layered, dense, overlapping elements, controlled disorder |
| **Retro-Futuristic**       | Neon accents, geometric shapes, CRT aesthetics            |
| **Organic/Natural**        | Soft curves, earth tones, hand-drawn elements             |
| **Luxury/Refined**         | Subtle animations, premium typography, restrained palette |
| **Editorial/Magazine**     | Strong grid, dramatic headlines, whitespace as feature    |
| **Brutalist/Raw**          | Exposed structure, harsh contrasts, anti-design           |
| **Art Deco/Geometric**     | Gold accents, symmetry, ornate patterns                   |
| **Soft/Pastel**            | Rounded corners, gentle gradients, friendly               |
| **Industrial/Utilitarian** | Functional, monospace, data-dense                         |

### 3. Define the Unforgettable Element

What's the ONE thing someone will remember? A hero animation? Typography treatment? Color combination? Unusual layout?

---

## Aesthetics Guidelines

### Typography — NEVER Generic

**BANNED**: Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts, Open Sans

**DO**: Distinctive, characterful choices that elevate the design.

| Use Case          | Approach                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Display/Headlines | Bold personality — Clash, Cabinet Grotesk, Satoshi, Space Grotesk (sparingly), Playfair Display |
| Body Text         | Refined readability — Instrument Sans, General Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans |
| Monospace/Code    | DM Mono, JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono                       |
| Pairing Strategy  | Contrast weights (thin display + bold body), contrast styles (serif + geometric sans) |

**Size Progression**: Use 3x+ jumps, not timid 1.5x increments.

### Color & Theme

**BANNED**: Purple gradients on white, evenly-distributed 5-color palettes

**DO**:

- **Dominant + Sharp Accent**: 70-20-10 rule (primary-secondary-accent)
- **CSS Variables**: `--primary`, `--accent`, `--surface`, `--text`
- **Commit to dark OR light**: Don't hedge with gray middle-grounds
- **High contrast CTAs**: Buttons should pop dramatically

```css
:root {
  --bg-primary: #0a0a0a;
  --bg-secondary: #141414;
  --text-primary: #fafafa;
  --text-secondary: #a1a1a1;
  --accent: #ff6b35;
  --accent-hover: #ff8555;
}
```

### Motion & Animation

**Priority**: One orchestrated page load > scattered micro-interactions

**High-Impact Moments**:

- Staggered hero reveals (`animation-delay`)
- Scroll-triggered section entrances
- Hover states that surprise (scale, color shift, shadow depth)
- Smooth page transitions

**Implementation**:

- CSS-only for simple animations
- Framer Motion for React (pre-installed via init scripts)
- Keep durations 200-400ms (snappy, not sluggish)

### Spatial Composition

**BANNED**: Centered, symmetrical, predictable layouts

**DO**:

- Asymmetry with purpose
- Overlapping elements
- Diagonal flow / grid-breaking
- Generous negative space OR controlled density (pick one)
- Off-grid hero sections

### Backgrounds & Atmosphere

**BANNED**: Solid white/gray backgrounds

**DO**:

- Gradient meshes (subtle, not garish)
- Noise/grain textures (SVG filter or CSS)
- Geometric patterns (dots, lines, shapes)
- Layered transparencies
- Dramatic shadows for depth
- Blur effects for glassmorphism

```css
/* Subtle grain overlay */
.grain::before {
  content: '';
  position: fixed;
  inset: 0;
  background: url("data:image/svg+xml,...") repeat;
  opacity: 0.03;
  pointer-events: none;
}
```

---

## Mobile-First Patterns

See **[references/mobile-patterns.md](references/mobile-patterns.md)** for detailed CSS.

### Critical Rules

| Pattern                 | Desktop           | Mobile Fix                                   |
| ----------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Hero with hidden visual | 2-column grid     | Switch to `display: flex` (not grid)         |
| Large selection lists   | Horizontal scroll | Accordion with category headers              |
| Multi-column forms      | Side-by-side      | Stack vertically                             |
| Status/alert cards      | Inline            | `align-items: center` + `text-align: center` |
| Feature grids           | 3-4 columns       | Single column                                |

### Breakpoints

```css
/* Tablet - stack sidebars */
@media (max-width: 1200px) { }

/* Mobile - full single column */
@media (max-width: 768px) { }

/* Small mobile - compact spacing */
@media (max-width: 480px) { }
```

### Font Scaling

```css
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .hero-title { font-size: 32px; }      /* from ~48px */
  .section-title { font-size: 24px; }   /* from ~32px */
  .section-subtitle { font-size: 14px; } /* from ~16px */
}
```

---

## Build Workflow

### Option A: Vite (Pure Static) — Recommended (Offline)

A pre-built Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui template with all dependencies is available at `/app/templates/vite-react`. Use it directly without network access:

```bash
# 1. Copy the pre-installed template
cp -r /app/templates/vite-react my-site
cd my-site

# 2. Develop — edit src/App.tsx, add components in src/components/
# All shadcn/ui components (button, badge, card, accordion, dialog,
# navigation-menu, tabs, sheet, separator, avatar, alert) are pre-installed.
# Framer Motion, Lucide icons, and Tailwind CSS are ready to use.

# 3. Build static files
npm run build
# Output: dist/

# 4. Bundle to single HTML (optional)
bash /app/skills/scripts/bundle-artifact.sh
# Output: bundle.html
```

### Option B: Init from Scratch (Requires Internet)

If internet access is available, you can scaffold from scratch:

```bash
# Vite
bash /app/skills/scripts/init-vite.sh my-site

# Next.js
bash /app/skills/scripts/init-nextjs.sh my-site
```

---

## Project Structure

### Vite Static (Pre-installed Template)

```
my-site/                      # copied from /app/templates/vite-react
├── src/
│   ├── components/
│   │   └── ui/              # Pre-installed shadcn/ui components
│   ├── lib/
│   │   └── utils.ts         # cn() helper for className merging
│   ├── styles/              # Global CSS
│   ├── config/
│   │   └── site.ts          # Editable content config
│   ├── App.tsx
│   └── main.tsx
├── index.html
├── components.json           # shadcn/ui config — required for adding components
├── tailwind.config.ts
├── vite.config.ts            # Path aliases (@/) configured
├── tsconfig.json
└── package.json
```

**`components.json`** is the shadcn/ui configuration file. It tells the `npx shadcn@latest add` CLI where to place components, which aliases to use, and the Tailwind CSS config path. It is pre-configured with:
- Style: `default`
- TSX: enabled, RSC: disabled (Vite, not Next.js)
- Aliases: `@/components`, `@/components/ui`, `@/lib`

### Next.js

```
my-site/
├── app/
│   ├── layout.tsx
│   ├── page.tsx
│   └── privacy/page.tsx
├── components/
├── lib/
├── config/
│   └── site.ts
└── tailwind.config.ts
```

## Site Config Pattern

Keep all editable content in one file:

```typescript
// config/site.ts
export const siteConfig = {
  name: "Acme AI",
  tagline: "Write better, faster",
  description: "AI-powered writing assistant",
  
  hero: {
```

## Pre-Implementation Checklist

Run this before finalizing any design:

### Design Quality

- [ ] Typography is distinctive (no Inter/Roboto/Arial)
- [ ] Color palette has clear dominant + accent (not evenly distributed)
- [ ] Background has atmosphere (not solid white/gray)
- [ ] At least one memorable/unforgettable element
- [ ] Animations are orchestrated (not scattered)

### Mobile Responsiveness

- [ ] Hero centers on mobile (no empty grid space)
- [ ] All grids collapse to single column
- [ ] Forms stack vertically
- [ ] Large lists use accordion (not horizontal scroll)
- [ ] Font sizes scale down appropriately

### Form Consistency

- [ ] Input, select, textarea all styled consistently
- [ ] Radio/checkbox visible (check transparent-border styles)
- [ ] Dropdown options have readable backgrounds
- [ ] Labels use CSS variables (not hardcoded colors)

### Accessibility

- [ ] Color contrast meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI)
- [ ] Focus states visible
- [ ] Semantic HTML (nav, main, section, article)
- [ ] Alt text for images
- [ ] Keyboard navigation works

---

## shadcn/ui Components

10 common components pre-installed (button, badge, card, accordion, dialog, navigation-menu, tabs, sheet, separator, avatar, alert). Add more with `npx shadcn@latest add [name]` or install all with `npx shadcn@latest add --all`.

See **[references/shadcn-components.md](references/shadcn-components.md)** for full component reference.

Most used for landing pages:

- `Button`, `Badge` — CTAs and labels
- `Card` — Feature cards, pricing tiers
- `Accordion` — FAQ sections
- `Dialog` — Modals, video players
- `NavigationMenu` — Header nav
- `Tabs` — Feature showcases
- `Carousel` — Testimonials

steps.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze the requirements and plan the build:

**Design Direction:**
- Tone: Luxury/Refined meets Editorial/Magazine - clean, contemporary SaaS
- Color: #141414 (primary dark text), #FFFFFF (bg), #F5F5F5 (light gray surface), electric violet accent
- Typography: Space Grotesk or Cabinet Grotesk for headlines, Plus Jakarta Sans for body
- Memorable element: The animated stat counters + smooth search tab switching + continuous marquee scrolls

**Sections (in order):**
1. Announcement bar
2. Hero (headline, subtitle, dual CTAs)
3. Trusted by (logo marquee)


4. Stats (animated counters)
5. Features - Search (tabs + filter pills + grid)
6. Features - Flows (Videos/Prototype toggle)
7. Features - Tools (3 cards)
8. Testimonials (multi-row auto-scrolling marquee)
9. CTA (with app icon marquee)
10. Footer

The key interactions I need to implement are the stats counters that animate on scroll, the search feature with tab switching and filter pills, the flows toggle between videos and prototypes, and the continuous marquee scrolls for testimonials and brand icons.

I'm going to create this as a single HTML file with embedded CSS and JavaScript since it needs to open directly in a browser without any build process. Given the requirement that index.html must be the main entry point in /app/output/, I'll write the complete self-contained file rather than using a build tool. I'm planning out the component structure for this landing page—I'll organize everything into a config file for content, a main App component for layout, and individual section components for each part like the hero, features, testimonials, and footer. There's a lot to build here, so I need to be strategic about keeping the code clean and efficient.

For the typography, the brief mentions Inter as a suggestion, but since that's restricted, I'll go with Plus Jakarta Sans for body text and Space Grotesk for headings—both are geometric sans-serifs that feel premium and distinctive while staying clean and readable.

The design direction is clearly Luxury/Refined based on the brief's emphasis on contemporary SaaS aesthetics with generous whitespace and crisp typography. For the accent color, I'm leaning toward a custom violet like #6C5CE7 rather than pure electric blue, which feels more sophisticated for this tone. Now I'm ready to start building the interface.

I'll set up the Vite template and work through the file structure systematically—starting with the Tailwind config to lock in the custom colors and fonts, then the site configuration, global styles with animations, and finally the main App component with all sections built inline to keep the file count manageable. I'm planning the implementation details for the interactive components—using IntersectionObserver for the stats counter animation, CSS keyframes for the marquee, and React state to manage tabs, toggles, and filter pills. Now I'm settling on the visual design with a clean white background, electric violet accents, and a mix of Space Grotesk for headlines and Plus Jakarta Sans for body text.

Writing the code files... I'm settling on a simpler approach—write everything in one large App.tsx file to minimize tool calls, then handle the build and output in a few bash commands.

Before I start coding, I need to check what the template provides and update the entry point files like main.tsx and index.html to wire everything up correctly. Let me copy the template first, scan the structure, then write out all the independent files in parallel before tackling the main component.

For App.tsx, I'm building a full landing page with an announcement bar at the top, followed by a header with navigation, a hero section with dual call-to-action buttons, a marquee of trusted company names, animated stat counters, a tabbed features section with screenshot grids, another features section toggling between video and prototype modes, three feature cards highlighting Figma integration and collaboration tools, a multi-row auto-scrolling testimonials marquee, a final CTA section, and a footer with navigation columns and social links.

I'll use a custom hook with IntersectionObserver and requestAnimationFrame for the animated counters, CSS keyframe animations for the marquees, and React state management for the interactive tabs, filters, and toggles. This is going to be a substantial component, so I'm aiming for around 800-1200 lines and structuring it with clear section components.

Building the App.tsx structure... Building the search feature section with tabs, filters, and a dynamic screenshot gallery...

Now I'm setting up the fonts from Google Fonts and structuring my workflow to copy the template, read the existing files, write all the modifications, build, and deploy to output. The design direction is clean and contemporary with a light theme—white backgrounds, near-black text, and subtle grays as accents.

For the color scheme, I'm going with a vibrant indigo (#6366F1) as the primary accent. The overall aesthetic should feel polished and refined like Linear or Notion, with no unnecessary decoration. The stats counter animation will be the standout interactive element with staggered timing and smooth easing, and the search section with its interactive tabs and pills will add another layer of engagement.

Building the React component with a custom hook for the count-up animation... Setting up the observer cleanup and then moving into the marquee animations with left and right keyframes that loop continuously, followed by the search tabs component structure.

Now I'm setting up the mock screenshot grid with colorful gradient backgrounds and UI elements to simulate a real app preview library.

I'll organize this efficiently by batching my tool calls: first copying the template, then reading the files I need to modify in parallel, writing all the changes together, and finally building and copying to output.

For the mock screenshots, I'm going to create more detailed mini UI mockups with phone frames, navigation bars, and content placeholders in different layouts to better showcase the product concept. I'll also need to figure out what to use for the Trusted By section since we don't have actual company logos.

Writing the App.tsx component now... lines
- TrustedBy: ~40 lines
- Stats: ~50 lines
- FeaturesSearch: ~200 lines (complex with tabs, pills, grid)
- FeaturesFlows: ~100 lines
- FeaturesTools: ~80 lines
- Testimonials: ~100 lines
- CTASection: ~100 lines
- Footer: ~80 lines
- App component: ~30 lines

Total: ~1000 lines. Manageable.

Let me start building this out now.

Actually, I should nail down the visual hierarchy first to ensure it feels premium. I'm mapping out each section's design approach: the announcement bar gets a violet background with white text and a subtle arrow, the header stays sticky with a frosted glass effect, and the hero section centers everything with a bold headline and supporting subtitle flanked by two button styles. The trusted companies section uses muted typography, stats display with counting animations, and the features are broken into three distinct patterns—a tabbed search interface with filterable pills, a toggle-based flows section, and a three-card tools layout. For testimonials and the CTA, I'm planning opposite-direction scrolling animations across two rows, plus another scrolling row of app icons. The footer follows a traditional multi-column structure. I'll alternate background colors throughout, starting with violet for the announcement, white for the hero, and continuing that pattern down the page.

Now I'm deciding on animation tech: Framer Motion handles scroll-triggered fades, tab transitions with AnimatePresence, and staggered card reveals, while CSS powers the marquee animations for better performance on continuous loops.

Building the component structure now. Writing component styles...

I'm settling on an indigo accent color with hover and focus states, then predefining the company logos for the trusted brands section and the marquee, using circular badges with initials and brand colors. For testimonials, I'll keep them simple with quote text, author name, and company. Time to actually build this out.

The Flows section will toggle between a video player mockup and an interactive prototype view with connected screens. I'm going with Space Grotesk for headlines and Plus Jakarta Sans for body text to keep things modern and distinctive. My plan is to set everything up first, write all the component files in parallel, then build and deploy.

Writing the implementation now...

steps.message:
The ScreenVault landing page is complete at `/app/output/index.html`.

**What was built:**
- Single-page landing site with all 10 sections from the brief (announcement bar, hero, trusted-by marquee, animated stats, search with tabs + filter pills, flows toggle, tools cards, testimonial marquees, CTA with brand marquee, footer)
- **6 interactive behaviors**: animated stat counters on scroll, search tab switching, filter pill selection, flows Videos/Prototype toggle, auto-scrolling testimonial marquee (2 rows, opposite directions), brand icon marquee
- Stack: React 18 + Tailwind CSS v4 + Framer Motion — built with Vite, output is static HTML/CSS/JS with relative paths
- Typography: Space Grotesk (headlines) + Plus Jakarta Sans (body), indigo accent (#6366F1), white/off-white/dark palette
- Fully responsive with mobile hamburger menu, adapted grids, and scaled typography
